The study by Blumenthal DS and Schultz MG in 1975 investigated the incidence of intestinal obstruction in children infected with Ascaris lumbricoides, published in the American Journal of Tropical Medicine and Hygiene. 2. De Silva NR, Guyatt HL, and Bundy DA in 1997 analyzed the morbidity and mortality associated with Ascaris-induced intestinal obstruction, as reported in the Transactions of the Royal Society of Tropical Medicine and Hygiene. 3. Baba AA, Ahmad SM, and Sheikh KA in 2009 identified intestinal ascariasis as the most common cause of bowel obstruction in children at a tertiary care center in Kashmir, published in Pediatric Surgery International. 4. Walsh JA and Warren KS in 1979 proposed selective primary healthcare as an interim strategy for disease control in developing countries, as detailed in the New England Journal of Medicine. 5. De Silva NR, Chan MS, and Bundy DA in 1997 re-estimated the global morbidity and mortality burden of ascariasis and conducted sensitivity analyses, published in Tropical Medicine and International Health. 6. Pawlowski ZS and Davis A in 1989 provided a comprehensive review of morbidity and mortality in ascariasis in their book published by Taylor & Francis in London. 7. Leonardi-Bee J, Pritchard D, and Britton J in 2006 conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis on the relationship between asthma and current intestinal parasite infections, published in the American Journal of Respiratory and Critical Care Medicine. 8. Lynch NR, Palenque M, Hagel I, and Di Prisco MC in 1997 reported clinical improvement of asthma following anthelmintic treatment in tropical settings, published in the American Journal of Respiratory and Critical Care Medicine. 9. Caraballo L and Acevedo N in 2011 discussed the impact of Ascaris lumbricoides infections as new allergens of relevance in tropical regions, published in the World Allergy Organization Journal. 10. Lee TD and Wright KA in 1978 described the morphology of the attachment and probable feeding site of the nematode Trichuris muris, published in the Canadian Journal of Zoology. 11. Bowie MD, Morison A, Ireland JD, and Duys PJ in 1978 explored the association between clubbing and whipworm infestation, published in the Archives of Disease in Childhood. 12. Zeehaida M, Zueter A, Zairi NZ, and Zunulhisham S in 2015 questioned whether enough is learned from case studies on Trichuris dysentery syndrome, published in Tropical Biomedicine. 13. Callender JE, Grantham-McGregor SM, Walter SP, and Cooper ES in 1994 evaluated treatment effects in Trichuris dysentery syndrome, published in Acta Paediatrica. 14. Noorizan AM and Mahendra Raj S in 2001 provided evidence suggesting that Trichuris dysentery syndrome may be underdiagnosed in Kelantan, published in the Medical Journal of Malaysia. 15. Cooper ES, Bundy DA, and Henry FJ in 1986 linked chronic dysentery, stunting, and whipworm infestation, published in The Lancet. 16. Azira NM and Zeehaida M in 2012 reported a case of severe chronic iron deficiency anemia secondary to Trichuris dysentery syndrome, published in Tropical Biomedicine. 17. Diniz-Santos DR, Jambeiro J, Mascarenhas RR, and Silva LR in 2006 described a case of massive Trichuris trichiura infection causing chronic bloody diarrhea in a child, published in the Journal of Tropical Pediatrics. 18. Hansen EP, Tejedor AM, Thamsborg SM, Alstrup-Hansen TV, Dahlerup JF, and Nejsum P in 2016 studied fecal egg counts and expulsion dynamics of Trichuris trichiura following self-infection, published in the Journal of Helminthology. 19. Khuroo MS, Khuroo MS, and Khuroo NS in 2010 identified Trichuris dysentery syndrome as a common cause of chronic iron deficiency anemia in adults in endemic areas, published in Gastrointestinal Endoscopy. 20. Krishnamurthy S, Samanta D, and Yadav S in 2009 reported a case of Trichuris dysentery syndrome with eosinophilic leukemoid reaction mimicking inflammatory bowel disease, published in the Journal of Postgraduate Medicine. 21. Zanwar VG, Pawar SV, Jain SS, Rathi SP, Contractor QQ, and Rathi PM in 2016 described an unusual case of overt gastrointestinal bleeding in a malnourished child, published in Tropical Doctor. 22. Layrisse M, Aparcedo L, Martinez-Torres C, and Roche M in 1967 quantified blood loss due to Trichuris trichiura infection, published in the American Journal of Tropical Medicine and Hygiene. 23. Robertson LJ, Crompton DW, Sanjur D, and Nesheim MC in 1992 examined hemoglobin concentrations and concurrent infections of hookworm and Trichuris trichiura in Panamanian primary school children, published in the Transactions of the Royal Society of Tropical Medicine and Hygiene. 24. Montresor A, Porta N, Albonico M, Gabrielli AF, Jankovic D, Fitzpatrick C, et al. in 2015 analyzed the relationship between prevalence and intensity classes of soil-transmitted helminthiasis, published in the Transactions of the Royal Society of Tropical Medicine and Hygiene. 25. Montresor A, Gabrielli AF, Yajima A, Lethanh N, Biggs BA, Casey GJ, et al. in 2013 used a Markov model to forecast changes in soil-transmitted helminth prevalence during a control program in Vietnam, published in the Transactions of the Royal Society of Tropical Medicine and Hygiene. 26. Joseph SA, Albonico M, Savioli L, Banger M, Montresor A, et al. in 2017 reviewed evidence on the efficacy of anthelmintics for large-scale drug administration to control soil-transmitted helminthiasis, published in PLoS Neglected Tropical Diseases. 27. Tun A, Myat SM, Gabrielli AF, and Montresor A in 2013 reported on the results of seven years of deworming to control soil-transmitted helminthiasis in Myanmar, published in Tropical Medicine and International Health. 28. Casey GJ, Jolly D, Phuc TQ, Tinh TT, Tho DH, Montresor A, et al. in 2010 demonstrated that long-term weekly iron-folic acid supplementation with deworming stabilizes hemoglobin and increases iron stores in non-pregnant women in Vietnam, published in PLoS One. 29. Sinuon M, Tsuyuoka R, Socheat D, Odermatt P, Ohmae H, Matsuda H, et al. in 2007 reported on eight years of control activities for Schistosoma mekongi in Cambodia, published in the Transactions of the Royal Society of Tropical Medicine and Hygiene. 30. Knopp S, Mohammed KA, Stothard JR, Khamis IS, Rollinson D, Marti H, et al. in 2010 studied patterns and risk factors of helminthiasis and anemia in Zanzibar in the context of helminth control programs, published in PLoS Neglected Tropical Diseases.
